Ethel Creek Falls Hike - Sun, 27th Oct 24 

Leader: Cherry Judge

Rated: On-Track hike. For the easy to moderately fit walkers who can walk about 3-4 hrs with a break 
 
Walk Description:
We will begin in Paluma village, making our way to Cloudy Creek.
Once we reach Cloudy Creek, we will cross the creek and then continue along a 'less travelled' track to Ethel Creek Falls.
We stop for morning tea and a swim at Ethel creek Falls.
Then we come back the same way. 
After the walk, if anyone is keen we can head to the cafe in Paluma for a post walk coffee.

If you have not walked with us before, please contact the walk leader before RSVP registration.

For more information, please contact the leader- Cherry Judge - info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.com

name: Tully Gorge Hike - Very Hard & Challenging
description:
Tully Gorge
Leader: Luen

Join us for a tough and exploratory hike up Tully Gorge. We’ll hike along the Tully River, clambering over boulders, and swim through cool water (pack swims) to the base of Tully Falls. From here, we'll be steeply ascending the spur into thick rainforest, where technical scrambling skills are required. From here, we'll navigate to the lookout track, around to the other side, and then descend off-track down the ridgeline to our cars.

The club have done this several times in the distant past, but this trip's leader hasn't; hence exploratory.  

Steep climbs, technical scrambling, and exposure to heights/cliff edges.
Off-track navigation through thick rainforest.
Requires high fitness and experience with scrambling/climbing.
This is a very hard, challenging hike. 
Be aware of heights, wet rocks, uneven ground.

Contact the walk leader to RSVP or for more information luenwarneke@gmail.com

name: Mt Marlow - Many Peaks Range - Intro Walk
description:
20th October (Sunday)
Many Peaks & Freshwater trails (Mt Marlow)

Where -  Many Peaks & Freshwater trails (Mt Marlow)

Led by - Cherry Judge 
Rated-  Level 2. You should have at least attempted Castle Hill. This is not for the absolute beginner , mainly due to the heat and time this walk will take. 

Duration (approx) of walking per day - Approximately 4 hours. 2km circuit.

Meeting place - At Pallarenda Park, at the end of Cape Pallarenda Rd, OUTSIDE the gates of the conservation park at 5:45 am for a 6 am start. 
Meeting Time . 5:45 am for a 6:00 am start 

About the walk:
On this hike we'll be heading up Lagoon trail  and walking along this flat trail for about 2 kms or so before taking the turn off  and making our way up the Many Peaks trail to the Mount Marlow summit. We'll take a few short stops along the way, and we will take a break at the top to take in the views. We will then come down Mt Marlow.

Approximate Time/Distance: 3-4 hours return , 12km circuit.

What to expect: Moderate level of fitness required. Expect some steep, uneven and rocky sections. 
There are exposed sections, so expect it to be hot. I cannot reiterate this enough - Bring plenty of hydration. 
The pace will be moderate and continuous, so we can cover the distance within the designated time-frame and enjoy our stops at the points of interest mentioned above.

If you are new to hiking hills, I would recommend doing Castle Hill first before you attempt Mt Marlow.
What to bring on the walk - https://bit.ly/wtbdayhike

Meeting point: Pallarenda Park, at the end of Cape Pallarenda Rd, OUTSIDE the gates of the conservation park at 5.30 am 

Information and maps for the Townsville Town Common Conservation Park:
https://wanderstories.space/cape-pallarenda/
https://parks.des.qld.gov.au/parks/townsville/

name: Williams Creek, Paluma
description:
Williams Creek Falls, Paluma Range NP
Saturday, October 12th to Sunday, October 13th, 2024
Led by Luen Warneke
Rated - Level 5 due to creek walk and how long the walk is. This walk is for moderately fit bushwalkers.
Duration - This walk is estimated to be a 6-8 hours each day.

Williams Creek winds its way down beside the K Traverse and has a rich history with the early European settlers of Paluma as well as the logging era. This lush rainforest creek is fairly easy to access and exit. The aqua-blue water and sandy area with small rocks and fern-filled contribute to the scenery and are typical for these rainforest creeks. You can see red claw yabbies, guppies, and various fungus types. There are small cascades along the way, one of which is the creek's main waterfall. This beautiful hike is varied in its landscape and vegetation. 
We will camp in the creek once we've had enough walking. Exit via Forgotten Falls Track or K Traverse (TBD). Hikers are required to book their own remote off-track camping permits via the QPWS booking portal website. Walkers without a camping permit will be rejected on the day. 
Contact the walk leader to discuss this overnight, off-track camp.
